title: Recipe and Locker
premise: Beatrix Delacroix transfers to Hollowmere Academy, a school built atop the ruins of a shuttered reform home, determined to stay invisible after a family scandal that cost them everything. When an anonymous group chat begins posting predictions that come true with eerie precision, Beatrix realizes the messages are being generated by something left behind in the building — and that his own locker is the anchor. As the predictions turn from pranks to threats, he uncovers that the chat's 'prophecies' are actually testimony: the voices of children who died at the old home, demanding justice the courts never gave. To free them, Beatrix must open the locker, expose the school's founding family's crimes, and accept that survival was never meant to be silent. In the end, the truth goes public, the dead are named, and Beatrix chooses to be seen.
about_author: Casper Montrose is the pen name of a former night-shift archivist who spent years cataloguing records of defunct institutions. They write young adult fiction about ordinary kids who inherit other people's secrets.

chapters.title: Head Down
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. His first week at Hollowmere Academy: keep grades up, keep the locker shut, keep out of everything. A tour guide mentions the school was built over 'the old Ashford Home,' and Beatrix feels the floor hum under his shoes. Emotional beat: the exhausting discipline of invisibility, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: The First Prediction
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He's added to a group chat called LOCKER 114 by mistake — or not. The first message predicts the gym flood two days early; it happens exactly as written. Nobody in the chat admits to sending it. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding caution, the thrill of being included for once.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He discovers Locker 114 is his own assignment — sealed shut since before he arrived, cold to the touch. The chat starts addressing him directly, using details only he knows. Emotional beat: dread braided with a strange feeling of being known.

chapters.title: The Ashford Home
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Priya, a fellow chat member and amateur local historian. Together they dig into records: the Ashford Home for 'wayward youth' closed in 1974 after a fire no one was ever charged for. Six names missing from every official list. Emotional beat: the chill of institutional erasure.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The chat escalates: it predicts a student's public humiliation, then makes it happen. Classmates start calling members 'the cult kids.' Beatrix's carefully built anonymity collapses as suspicion lands on him. Emotional beat: the price of proximity to the truth.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. In the county archive, Priya finds a survivor's letter naming Headmaster Corwin Ashford's grandson — now the school's beloved benefactor — as the one who locked the dorm doors. The chat sends its first threat aimed at a living person. Emotional beat: righteous anger meeting real danger.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The chat offers him a deal: help expose the Ashfords and it will erase the record of his family's scandal — give him back a clean name. He realizes the entity can trade in secrets because it was built from stolen ones. Emotional beat: temptation, and recognizing his own hunger for erasure.

chapters.title: Time Already Running Out
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The final prediction arrives with a countdown: on the fire's anniversary, the west wing burns again, with students inside, unless the six names are read aloud in assembly. The school locks down; the benefactor moves to destroy the archive. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, climax. During Founders' Day assembly, Beatrix takes the stage, opens Locker 114's twin — the old home's intake ledger — and reads the six names aloud as smoke curls through the vents. Students film; the benefactor lunges; the chat floods every screen with the evidence. Emotional beat: courage as choosing to be seen.

chapters.title: Grades Up, Locker Open
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, resolution. The investigation breaks open; the Ashford name is stripped from the school. The chat goes quiet, then sends one last message: thank you, signed with all six names. Beatrix leaves his locker open on purpose. Emotional beat: grief, release, and the beginning of a life lived unhidden.
